objectives.text: Name the features that help a cactus survive in a hot, dry desert, explain how camouflage keeps an animal safe from hungry birds, and explain why birds migrate and when they return
successCriteria: I can name the cactus features: a thick stem that stores water, sharp thorns that stop thirsty animals, and deep roots that find water
I can explain that the moth's wings match the tree bark, so hungry birds cannot spot it
I can explain that birds migrate thousands of kilometres to warmer places for winter and return when spring brings food back
assessmentPoints: Cactus-feature answers in the opening activity
Camouflage and migration answers in the second and third activities

objectives.text: Say why animal features are not chosen on purpose - they developed over many, many generations, not by choice - and say what happens to forest animals when people clear the trees
successCriteria: I can say that features developed over many, many generations, not by choice
I can say that when the trees go, the animals lose their food and shelter and must move away
assessmentPoints: Trap discussion in the opening activity
Forest-clearing answers in the fourth activity and the closing practice

activities.title: The cactus: built for the hot, dry desert
Blending in keeps the moth safe

differentiation.support: Provide a simple route map with arrows so learners can follow the flock's journey south and back before explaining migration themselves.

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why the cactus's well-fitting features still do not show it chose to grow them.
